rv.q: "Gorgeous" is worth seeing for its vividly rendered characters and its thoughtful exploration of grief, loneliness and the complicated legacy of one man for the women who survive him.
“Gorgeous” by Rivendell and Raven Theatre is heartbreaking, hilarious and engrossing, a hit to kick off the summer season.
Keiko Green’s story of love, loss and a sweet little bulldog will warm every theatergoer’s heart and stir their soul.
Raven Theatre and Rivendell Theatre Ensemble's coproduction of this world premiere, directed by Kirsten Fitzgerald, is an excellent balance of the bitter and the sweet.
The costumes by Maegan Pate and the fight choreography by Stephanie Mattos were perfect making the total production one that I would call flawless.

cn.t: Green's charming two-hander about opposites colliding earns praise for its funny, sweet balance of bitter and sweet, though it follows a familiar template. Strong performances elevate this world premiere co-production.
